newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Swedbank builds Swedish bank giant.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Swedbank builds Swedish bank giant.

text.p: Swedish banks Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced their marriage on Tuesday after saying on Monday they were in merger talks.
The merger will create Sweden's second biggest bank after the recently merged Handelsbanken and Stadshypotek, with a large retail customer base and strong rural presence.

Analysts expected the amalgamation to drive S-E-Banken and Nordbanken back into merger negotiations that collapsed two weeks ago, which would create a third large Swedish bank with the strength to compete against big European rivals.
"The boards of Foreningsbanken and Sparbanken (the name Swedbank uses in Sweden) have decided to propose a merger and form ForeningsSparbanken," the two banks said in a statement.
Under the merger agreement, two shares in the new banks will be given for every seven A-shares in Foreningsbanken.
The banks told a press conference merger costs would be 2.0 billion crowns ($268.2 million) at the most and savings of 1.5 billion crowns a year would be achieved by the year 2000.
This would include axing about 2,000 jobs from the combined workforce of around 14,000.
Trading in the two banks, suspended before the markets opened on Monday, was to resume at 1400 GMT.

The merger announcement came as no real surprise to the market as Swedbank's interest in Foreningsbanken has been widely known since 1994 and has become more intense under the current restructuring of Sweden's banking sector.
Foreningsbanken, which has a large rural customer base and is 20 percent owned by farmers' associations, spurned advances by the bigger bank last June.
Swedbank had bought up about 5.0 percent of the shares of Foreningsbanken and wanted the two banks to have close co-operation, but the farmers' association was opposed to the relationship.
"So the merger has not come as any real surprise," said one London-based banking analyst.
"It should even get interest up again in a possible merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken (talks which collapsed two weeks ago)."
The merged bank will be the second largest in Sweden with combined assets of 657 billion crowns, compared with Handelsbanken/Stadhypoteks assets of 870 billion crowns.
"The merger was very much expected with everyone waiting for it and it will be positive for the market," said analyst Peter Thorn from Paribas. "Now they need to get down to cost savings."
Swedbank and Foreningsbanken both posted their 1996 results on Tuesday morning.
Swedbank's result was better than expected with a 20 percent lift in operating profit to 5.30 billion crowns. The market had expected a profit of 4.99 billion crowns.
Foreningsbanken's result was in line with expectations. It reported a 14 percent increase in operating profit to 1.16 billion crowns against expectations of 1.13 billion crowns.

Another of Sweden's big four banks, Handelsbanken also posted its 1996 results, announcing a 33 percent jump in operating profit to 6.72 billion crowns. This was above market expectations of a profit of 6.03 billion crowns.
"Swedish banks are definitely back on recovery," said Thorn.
"The question now is how they can continue to maintain the momentum."
($ = 7.456 Swedish Crowns)
